quote:
A century that burns bright does so not by the fireworks that explode, but by the inner flame that refuses to gutter with age.

Even the most iron-clad walls of commerce can be raided by waves of discord, yet true strength lies in the roots that stay buried beneath.

When the sky threatens to tumble into a storm, those who find refuge first learn that the greatest barometer is the steadiness of their own breath.

Freedom finally sounds once the stone cage creaks, but the real prison held is that of superstition, and its key is faith unshackled by fear.

On a chessboard the grandmaster's mind is the only weapon that can outmaneuver any opponent, for games played with honesty never betray the soul.

When a life reaches its final stop, the earth itself listens as the wind transcribes the lessons of those who walked beside it.

Heat that scorches the surface can also cool the spirit if one only harbors patience the way the horizon insists on ever returning.
